vela_comparison.convention: Native normalized population columns; fixed transport diagonal row calibration for the diagnostic, not an absolute-unit or global RHS equivalence claim.

interpretation: The tested continuous printed linear system does not equal the literal derivative of RHS1 with respect to the logged populations.
The same-state fresh full derivative predicts the one-sided and symmetric RHS responses.
The continuous effective matrix numerically matches a control with -Derivatives and -AvalDerivatives while the physical RHS and AV generation remain enabled.
Differences also occur for unprotected controls; concentration in previously protected columns alone does not prove a special protected-column algorithm.
limitations: Numerical equivalence identifies this step effective linearization; the internal reason for its phase/iteration behavior is not established.
Only selected columns and rows were directionally perturbed; no global native Jacobian qualification is claimed.
Vela comparisons use declared fixed transport diagonal row calibration and keep its material/constants differences.
No new production code, population projection, fixed QF cap or stopping-rule change; no new complete BV run.
